title: Inquiry into police shooting death makes no recommendations
article: A provincial court judge in Edmonton has decided not to make any recommendations for change after holding an inquiry into a March 2005 shooting in which police killed a man who approached them with a knife.
Daniel Lippa, 29, was shot seven times outside his north-side apartment building after his estranged wife called 911 to say Lippa had threatened to kill her and her child.

In her report, released Friday, Alberta Provincial Court Judge Elizabeth Johnson accepted the evidence given by four police officers at the inquiry in March 2007. They testified they fired at Lippa after he refused to drop his knife and advanced on officers who told him to stop.

The judge also rejected the statement of another witness, who said she watched the incident from her second-storey bedroom window and didn't see Lippa carrying a knife or aggressively approaching the officers, "as honest, but mistaken."
The judge did not reach any conclusion as to why Lippa attacked the officers.
"Mr. Lippa was clearly distraught that evening. He had consumed alcohol but ... it would be speculative to address what his intentions might have been," she wrote.
